result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`"java"`, `"js"`), and the landscape merges legacy `"  *.java"` data into the same entries. All 330 `codeanalyzer` tests pass offline. I did not run the `reports` or `codeexplorer` tests, and I did not commit.

What changed:

- **`SourceCodeAspectUtils.getAspectsPerExtensions`** creates the per-extension aspects as `"java"` instead of `"  *.java"`. This also changes the scope names from `getScopesWithExtensions()`.
- **`AnalysisUtils.analyze`** builds the `_EXT_` metric ids from the bare name, so `NUMBER_OF_FILES_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` and `LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` are unchanged. The indented `  *.java: N files, …` summary line keeps its look.
- **`LandscapeAnalysisResults`** has a new `getExtensionName` helper that strips a leading `*.` and lower-cases the rest. It is used in the per-repository loop and in `merge()`, so the main scope and the merged "other" category combine both spellings. Each merged entry still gets one description per contributing repository.
- **Tests:** `CodeConfigurationTest` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` now assert the bare names.

I left the report-side `.replace("*.", "")` calls in `reports/` in place. They are no-ops on the new names, so removing them is a separate cleanup I did not make.
